definition: Educational robotics teaches the design, analysis, application and operation of robots.
details: Robots include articulated robots, mobile robots or autonomous vehicles. Educational robotics can be taught from elementary school to graduate programs. Robotics may also be used to motivate and facilitate the instruction other, often foundational, topics such as computer programming, artificial intelligence or engineering design.

explainer.lead: Educational robotics uses robots as something to study, build and operate. It can introduce robotics itself or make subjects such as programming, artificial intelligence and engineering design more engaging, from elementary school through graduate study.

tiers.eli5: Educational robotics means learning by working with robots, a bit like learning how bicycles work by riding one and trying its parts. You might build a small moving robot, tell it what to do, and see whether your instructions work. It can teach both robotics and skills such as programming and design.
tiers.practitioner: Educational robotics can be applied through articulated robots, mobile robots or autonomous vehicles, with activities matched to learners from elementary school to graduate programs. A course can focus on robot design, analysis, application and operation, or use robot projects to teach programming, artificial intelligence and engineering design. A key pitfall is letting the robot activity become an end in itself without connecting its results to the concepts being taught.
tiers.paperLevel: Educational robotics is the teaching of robot design, analysis, application and operation, using systems such as articulated robots, mobile robots and autonomous vehicles. It spans elementary through graduate education and can also serve as an instructional setting for computer programming, artificial intelligence and engineering design. Its scope therefore includes both robotics as the subject of study and robotics as a means of motivating other foundational subjects.

explainer.example: A class could build a small mobile robot, write a program that makes it move through a marked course, and then test and revise its design. The activity teaches robot operation while giving learners practice in programming and engineering design.

explainer.intuition: A robot gives learners a physical system whose design, instructions and behaviour they can examine together. That makes robotics useful both as a subject in its own right and as a practical setting for learning other technical subjects.
howItWorks: Choose a robot, such as an articulated robot, mobile robot or autonomous vehicle.
Study or develop aspects of its design and application.
Give it instructions or operate it in an activity suited to the learners.
Analyse what happens and connect the result to robotics or a foundational topic.
explainer.whyItMatters: It provides a way to teach robotics at many educational levels while also motivating foundational subjects. Learners can connect design and programming decisions with the observable behaviour of a robot.
misconceptions: It is not limited to university study; it can begin in elementary school.
Its purpose is not only to teach robotics: it can also support programming, artificial intelligence and engineering design.
